page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Dadv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The configuration provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It features 256 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) for vector and deep learning workloads, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with Geekbench multi-core and image processing scores reaching top-tier status. Memory performance shows a distinct tradeoff: cached small-block read bandwidth is exceptionally high at 4863.97 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to an average 153.37 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth remains strong at 108.24 GB/sec. The instance also demonstrates strong database performance, processing 88.8 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring highly in Passmark database operations.

Given its high resource density, dedicated CPU allocation, and substantial local storage, the D64ads_v6 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring balanced compute and memory without the overhead of a GPU. It is highly suited for relational databases, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.

Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core performance and image processing, alongside strong database capabilities, including 88.8 million Redis SET operations per second. It is highly suited for database hosting, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference.
